newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Several reformers promoted in reshuffle - Russian PM.
newsitem.headline: Several reformers promoted in reshuffle - Russian PM.

text.p: Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said in televised remarks on Monday that several reformers had been promoted in the new Russian government.

Deputy Economy Minister Yakov Urinson became a Deputy Prime Minister and Economy Minister and the head of the State Property Committee -- Russia's privatisation minister -- Alfred Kokh also became a Deputy Prime Minister. The more conservative Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov retained his position of Deputy Prime Minister.

Earlier this month Yeltsin, angered by the failure to end chronic delays in wages and pensions which were stoking public discontent, ordered Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin to reshape the government and improve its performance.

Last week Yeltsin named his reformist chief-of-staff Anatoly Chubais as first deputy prime minister. Earlier on Monday, the liberal governor of Nizhny Novgorod region, Boris Nemtsov, got a similar job alongside Chubais.

Chernomyrdin said that the mayor of Samara on the Volga river, Oleg Sysuyev, and reformist Communications Minister Vladimir Bulgak also became deputy prime ministers. Deputy Prime Minister Valery Serov, who is in charge of dealing with other former Soviet republics, kept his post.
Chernomyrdin said that some ministerial portfolios were still vacant and will be filled within a week.
